beatHypothesis.assay: Run the shipped reference agent (tidepool's `npm run bot`, or farstone's documented headless POST /connect + POST /command sequence) against a live world instance while a human is connected through the browser client; confirm the agent's presence and actions are visible in the human's Surroundings/Transcript pane via the documented protocol, with zero ToS exposure -- versus the same behavior on Achaea or Aardwolf, where it is named and prohibited in the incumbent's own first-party policy text.
beatHypothesis.outcome: An autonomous agent can inhabit the same persistent, multiplayer room as a human browser player and act through a documented, versioned protocol as an accepted, intended mode of play -- not a policy-risked or bannable one -- and a human visitor can observe that agent's presence and actions through the ordinary browser UI.
beatHypothesis.structuralFact: Farstone and Tidepool ship a first-party, documented, versioned agent entry point as an intended, first-class mode of play alongside the browser -- Farstone's headless JSON-over-HTTP world adapter (POST /connect, POST /command, POST /tick, GET /events -- catalog-entry.json) and Tidepool's WS tidepool.protocol.v1 with a shipped reference-agent bot ('agents and humans as first-class players alike', 'npm run bot runs the reference agent player') -- not an emergent scripting layer bolted onto a human-oriented ANSI stream. Achaea and Aardwolf, by contrast, govern trigger/automation/bot use as against-the-rules by first-party policy: Aardwolf states verbatim 'Any method which provides your character with gains, without meaningful interaction from you, is illegal... Full-fledged bots...are not tolerated and will be removed on sight, with no excuse' (aardwolf.com/wiki, policy updated 2024-02-19); Achaea maintains a dedicated governed help section, '15.8 Triggers -- Triggers, Automation, and Auto' (achaea.com/game-help).

v.receiverSentence: A player who wants an inhabitable persistent text world entrusts the surface with taking them from a bare URL to inhabiting a shared, persistent room they can act in and be seen in, in under two minutes, using only a browser -- bounded to live browser-playable MUDs a new player could join today, not client downloads, not single-player interactive fiction, and not the upstream engines (FeltOS/QwzSpace) that make the surface possible.
v.surprises: Alter Aeon's own play page still literally embeds a Flash .swf and its meta description says 'Requires Adobe Flash support' -- with a server Last-Modified header of June 2026, i.e. the page has been touched recently without anyone removing a client that has been non-functional in every mainstream browser since Adobe's January 2021 Flash end-of-life; house notes/model memory would have called this 'a browser client' had it not been directly fetched. tidepool.561.group's live 503 ('The service you requested is not available yet. Please try again in 30 seconds.') matched the task brief's own description exactly -- confirms the concurrent-lot framing rather than surfacing a new defect. Farstone's entry flow needs only a name and no password, which is genuinely faster than any incumbent's onboarding but is a real, unflagged identity-security gap (name-squatting/impersonation), not a pure win -- recorded as a MEET gap rather than folded into the BEAT claim. Both measured incumbents govern automation/bots as an enforcement problem against their own player base rather than as a designed capability, which is stronger evidence for the agent-symmetry BEAT hypothesis than anything found in house vocabulary alone.
